name: Luray Caverns
blurb: Largest show cave in the East: a paved 1.25-mile loop past Dream Lake, Giant's Hall and the Great Stalacpipe Organ, which plays the stalactites. The ticket also covers the Car and Carriage Caravan museum.

name: Skyline Caverns
blurb: One-hour guided tour of a cave known for anthodites, rare needle-like white crystal clusters on the ceiling, plus underground streams and the 37-foot Rainbow Falls.

name: Shenandoah Caverns
blurb: Hour-long guided tour reached by elevator, the only Virginia show cave with one, known for its striped 'bacon' formations. The parade-float warehouse next door is seasonal (closed since Sept 7).

name: Endless Caverns
blurb: Guided tour through winding passages lit mostly in white light. More than five miles have been surveyed and no end to the cave has been found.

name: Grand Caverns
blurb: America's oldest continuously operated show cave, open since 1806. The 70-minute tour passes rare shield formations, Cathedral Hall and signatures left by Civil War soldiers.

name: Melrose Caverns
blurb: Small family-run cave north of Harrisonburg where Civil War soldiers camped and carved names and drawings into the walls. Guided tours leave every 90 minutes.

name: Crystal Grottoes Caverns
blurb: Maryland's only show cave, found by quarry blasting in 1920. A guided walk of about 40 minutes through narrow passages densely packed with stalactites, columns and flowstone.

facts.hours: Daily 10-5 Apr 17-Nov 30; Fri-Sun Dec 1-14; groups by reservation only mid-Dec to mid-Mar

name: Indian Echo Caverns
blurb: 45-minute guided tour of a limestone cave on Swatara Creek near Hershey, 52 degrees year-round, with the story of the 'Pennsylvania Hermit' who lived inside for 19 years.

name: Lincoln Caverns & Whisper Rocks
blurb: Two separate caves on one ticket, Lincoln Caverns and Whisper Rocks, with flowstone, crystals and winding passages; about an hour underground with a guide.

name: Lost River Caverns
blurb: Five-chamber limestone cave with an underground stream whose source and outlet are unknown. The 30-45 minute guided tour starts from a lobby with a rock, mineral and fossil museum.

name: Crystal Cave
blurb: Pennsylvania's oldest show cave, discovered in 1871; a 55-minute guided tour past crystal-lined formations. Seasonal, so check dates before driving.

facts.hours: Seasonal (roughly Mar-Nov); check site for dates

name: Howard Peters Rawlings Conservatory
blurb: 1888 Victorian Palm House and connected greenhouses in Druid Hill Park: orchid, Mediterranean, tropical and desert rooms. Warm and dry in any weather.

name: United States Botanic Garden Conservatory
blurb: Glass conservatory at the foot of the Capitol: a jungle room crossed by a canopy walkway, plus desert, orchid, primeval and medicinal plant houses.

name: Brookside Gardens Conservatory
blurb: Two connected conservatories in Wheaton Regional Park with tropical plants and changing seasonal displays; the visitor center and its exhibits are a short walk away.

name: Longwood Gardens Conservatory
blurb: Acres under glass: the 2024 West Conservatory set on a pool, the Orchid House, palm and fern houses and a 10,010-pipe organ in the ballroom. Easily half a day indoors.

name: Hershey Gardens Conservatory & Butterfly Atrium
blurb: The Milton & Catherine Hershey Conservatory holds a year-round indoor Butterfly Atrium with hundreds of tropical butterflies; 23 acres of gardens outside.

name: Hillwood Estate, Museum & Gardens
blurb: Marjorie Merriweather Post's mansion: Faberge eggs, Russian imperial art and French decorative arts, plus a working greenhouse full of orchids.

facts.hours: Tue-Sun 10-5; closed Mon and several weeks in January

name: National Aquarium
blurb: Multi-level aquarium on Pier 3: Atlantic coral reef and shark ring tanks, a glass-roofed tropical rain forest, an Australian river gorge and a jellyfish gallery.

name: George Peabody Library
blurb: 1878 library with a 61-foot skylit atrium ringed by five tiers of cast-iron balconies holding 300,000 books. Visitors may walk into the reading room floor and take photos.

facts.hours: Closed to visitors on Fridays; check the hours page

name: Library of Congress, Thomas Jefferson Building
blurb: The Great Hall's marble staircases and mosaics, the Main Reading Room overlook, a Gutenberg Bible and Thomas Jefferson's own library.

name: Washington National Cathedral
blurb: Gothic cathedral with a Space Window holding a moon rock, crypt chapels, the tomb of Woodrow Wilson and hundreds of carvings. Sightseeing hours shift around services.

name: Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception
blurb: Largest Catholic church in North America: a Byzantine-Romanesque upper church covered in mosaics above the low-vaulted Crypt Church and more than 80 chapels.

name: Baltimore Basilica
blurb: America's first Catholic cathedral, finished in 1821 to Benjamin Latrobe's design: a skylit dome above, and an undercroft of brick inverted arches with the archbishops' crypt.

facts.hours: Open daily; closes 1 pm on weekdays

name: Franciscan Monastery of the Holy Land
blurb: Guided tour through full-size replicas of Holy Land shrines, then down into dim replica Roman catacombs under the church. The cloister and church are open without a tour.

facts.hours: Tours Tue, Wed, Fri, Sat at 1 and 2; Sun at 12 and 1:30; no Mon or Thu tours

name: National Building Museum (Great Hall)
blurb: The Great Hall of the 1887 Pension Building: a 316-foot atrium with eight 75-foot Corinthian columns, among the tallest interior columns anywhere. The hall is free.

name: Bromo Seltzer Arts Tower
blurb: 1911 clock tower modeled on Florence's Palazzo Vecchio, with artist studios on 15 floors, a Bromo-Seltzer bottle museum and tours inside the working clock room.

name: Maryland State House
blurb: Oldest state capitol in continuous legislative use. See the Old Senate Chamber where Washington resigned his commission, under the largest wooden dome built without nails.

name: U.S. Naval Academy Chapel & Crypt of John Paul Jones
blurb: Domed chapel with Tiffany windows; beneath it John Paul Jones lies in a marble sarcophagus held up by bronze dolphins. Preble Hall's ship models are a short walk away.

facts.hours: Walk in at the Gate 1 visitor center with REAL ID; no visitor vehicles

name: Pennsylvania State Capitol
blurb: 1906 capitol with a dome modeled on St. Peter's, a Moravian tile floor by Henry Mercer and Violet Oakley murals, shown on free guided tours.

facts.hours: Tours every half hour Mon-Fri 8:30-4; weekends at 9, 11, 1 and 3

name: Masonic Temple of Philadelphia
blurb: 1873 temple beside City Hall with seven lodge halls, each in a different style: Egyptian, Norman, Gothic, Ionic, Corinthian, Renaissance and Oriental. Seen by guided tour.

facts.hours: Guided tours only, Wed-Sat at 10, 11, 1, 2 and 3

name: George Washington Masonic National Memorial
blurb: 333-foot tower modeled on the ancient Lighthouse of Alexandria. Tours ride slanted elevators past a replica lodge room and Washington relics to an observation deck.

facts.hours: Thu-Mon; guided tours at 9:30, 11, 12:30, 2 and 3:30; closed federal holidays

name: Kogod Courtyard (American Art Museum & National Portrait Gallery)
blurb: Two museums share the old Patent Office Building and its glass-roofed Kogod Courtyard, a dry place to sit. Upstairs are the tiled Great Hall and the visible-storage Luce Center.

name: Glencairn Museum
blurb: Castle-like 1930s home built for Raymond Pitcairn's collection: medieval stained glass and sculpture, Egyptian, Greek and Roman antiquities and a mosaic-lined great hall.

name: Fonthill Castle
blurb: Henry Mercer's 1912 poured-concrete castle: 44 rooms, 18 fireplaces and 32 stairwells, with his handmade tiles set into nearly every surface. Seen by guided tour.

facts.hours: Tue-Sun 10-5; closed Mon; some early closings for private events

name: Mercer Museum
blurb: Six-story concrete castle holding some 50,000 pre-industrial tools. A whaleboat, wagons and a gallows hang in the open central court.

name: Folger Shakespeare Library
blurb: Home of the world's largest Shakespeare collection, with a gallery displaying all 82 of its First Folios, a Tudor-style Great Hall cafe and an Elizabethan theatre.

name: The Mansion on O Street
blurb: Joined row houses with more than 100 rooms and some 70 secret doors, crammed with memorabilia. You wander on your own hunting for the hidden doors.

name: National Shrine of Saint Elizabeth Ann Seton
blurb: Basilica holding the tomb of the first U.S.-born saint, a museum and visitor center opened in 2023, and the Stone House and White House where she lived and taught.

name: Hampton National Historic Site
blurb: Georgian mansion that was the largest private house in America when finished in 1790. Rangers lead tours of the furnished rooms; slave quarters and farm buildings nearby.

name: Westminster Hall Catacombs & Poe's Grave
blurb: Edgar Allan Poe is buried in the churchyard. The 1852 church was raised on brick arches over older graves, creating catacombs you can enter on monthly tours.

facts.hours: Catacomb tours first Saturday of the month at 11 and 1; burying ground daily 9-5

name: Dupont Underground
blurb: Abandoned 1949 streetcar station and curved platforms under Dupont Circle, reused as an art space. Open only when an exhibition or event is on.

facts.hours: Gallery hours Fri 4-7:30, Sat-Sun 11-5 during exhibitions

name: Eastern State Penitentiary
blurb: Crumbling 1829 radial prison with vaulted, skylit cellblocks, Al Capone's cell and death row, toured with an audio guide. Mostly under roof but unheated.

name: National Archives Rotunda
blurb: The Rotunda displays the original Declaration of Independence, Constitution and Bill of Rights under dim light; a 1297 Magna Carta is in the galleries.

name: American Visionary Art Museum
blurb: Self-taught and outsider art across three buildings: obsessive, strange and funny works, kinetic sculpture, a 55-foot whirligig and a mirror-mosaic exterior.

name: Baltimore Museum of Industry
blurb: An 1865 oyster cannery on the harbor with a belt-driven machine shop, garment loft, print shop and cannery line, and the 1906 steam tug Baltimore at the pier.

name: B&O Railroad Museum (National Museum of Railroad History & Innovation)
blurb: Birthplace of American railroading, now renamed: the 1884 roundhouse with a 22-sided dome full of 19th-century locomotives, plus more engines in the car shops.

name: Historic Ships in Baltimore
blurb: Go below decks on the 1854 sloop-of-war Constellation, the WWII submarine Torsk, Coast Guard cutter 37 and the lightship Chesapeake. Seven Foot Knoll Lighthouse is closed for now.

name: Walters Art Museum
blurb: Free museum of mummies, armor, medieval ivories and illuminated manuscripts, with a recreated Chamber of Wonders, a 1600s nobleman's cabinet of curiosities.

facts.hours: Check site for open days (not confirmed)

name: Baltimore Museum of Art
blurb: Free museum with the Cone Collection, the largest public holding of Matisse, plus African art, period rooms and Roman mosaics from Antioch.

name: Baltimore Streetcar Museum
blurb: Car barn of restored Baltimore streetcars from the horsecar era to the 1940s; a visit includes rides along the old Ma & Pa right of way on Falls Road.

facts.hours: Sundays 11-5 from Sept 1 to Dec 1; closed Jan-Feb

name: Fire Museum of Maryland
blurb: More than 40 fire engines, from 1806 hand pumpers to mid-century trucks, plus a working fire-alarm telegraph office.

name: Edgar Allan Poe House & Museum
blurb: The small brick row house where Poe lived in the 1830s and began writing fiction, with narrow winder stairs up to his garret room.

name: Star-Spangled Banner Flag House
blurb: The 1793 house where Mary Pickersgill sewed the Star-Spangled Banner in 1813, with a small museum on the flag next door.

name: National Great Blacks In Wax Museum
blurb: More than 100 life-size wax figures tell Black history, including a walk-through replica of a slave ship's hold.

name: Jewish Museum of Maryland & Lloyd Street Synagogue
blurb: Tour the 1845 Lloyd Street Synagogue, the third-oldest standing synagogue in the U.S., with its excavated mikveh, plus changing exhibits.

name: Maryland Aviation Museum (Glenn L. Martin)
blurb: Glenn L. Martin Company history at the old Middle River plant: models, engines and photographs, with aircraft on the flight line. Recently moved; the entrance is at the rear.

facts.hours: Check site for hours (not confirmed after the move)

name: SS John W. Brown
blurb: One of two WWII Liberty ships still able to sail. Tours cover the triple-expansion steam engine room, crew quarters, bridge and gun tubs.

facts.hours: Tours most Wed and Sat, starting 9 am

name: National Cryptologic Museum
blurb: NSA's public museum beside Fort Meade: Enigma machines you can try, Navajo code talker and Cold War cipher gear, and early supercomputers.

facts.hours: Tue-Fri 10-4 plus first Saturday of the month; closed federal holidays

name: Annapolis Maritime Museum
blurb: In the last oyster packing plant in Annapolis: exhibits on oystering, watermen and Bay ecology, with aquarium tanks and a view over Back Creek.

name: Banneker-Douglass-Tubman Museum
blurb: Maryland's museum of African American history, built around the brick 1875 Mount Moriah AME Church; changing art and history exhibitions.

name: Historic London Town & Gardens
blurb: Visitor center exhibit on the lost colonial port with artifacts dug on site, and the c.1760 brick William Brown House on the South River. The gardens are outdoors.

name: Robinson Nature Center
blurb: Exhibits on local habitats, a domed planetarium and a discovery room, in a building above the Middle Patuxent River.

name: Oregon Ridge Nature Center
blurb: Exhibits on local wildlife and the iron ore and marble once dug at Oregon Ridge, with live reptiles and amphibians and a glass-walled beehive.

name: Marshy Point Nature Center
blurb: Live turtles, snakes and tanks of upper Bay fish, with exhibits on the Dundee and Saltpeter Creek marshes; a short path leads down to the water.

name: Havre de Grace Decoy Museum
blurb: More than 1,200 working and decorative decoys and the tools of the Susquehanna Flats carvers, with figures of the carvers in a recreated workshop.

name: Havre de Grace Maritime Museum
blurb: Upper Bay boatbuilding, fishing and Underground Railroad exhibits, a wooden boat shop and an environmental center, a block from Concord Point Lighthouse.

name: Fort McHenry National Monument
blurb: The visitor center film ends with the flag revealed through the window. Then walk the star fort's brick barracks, powder magazine and bombproofs.

name: Lexington Market
blurb: Public market founded in 1782, in a new market shed since 2022: Faidley's crab cakes and dozens of food stalls under one roof.

name: Jericho Covered Bridge
blurb: 1865 Burr arch covered bridge still carrying cars over the Little Gunpowder Falls, beside the stone buildings of Jerusalem Mill village.

name: NASA Goddard Visitor Center
blurb: Small free NASA museum: Hubble and Webb telescope exhibits, a Science on a Sphere globe theater, a Gemini capsule model and a rocket garden outside.

name: National Wildlife Visitor Center (Patuxent Research Refuge)
blurb: Large exhibit hall on wildlife research, habitats and endangered species such as the whooping crane, with viewing windows over Lake Redington.

name: College Park Aviation Museum
blurb: On the world's oldest continuously operating airport (1909): Wright-era aircraft, early mail planes and hands-on flight simulators in one bright hangar.

name: National Capital Trolley Museum
blurb: Streetcars from Washington and European cities in a display hall, a model of a 1930s streetcar line, and rides on a mile of track through the woods.

name: National Museum of Health and Medicine
blurb: Army medical museum begun in 1862: the bullet that killed Lincoln, skeletal and brain specimens, a human hairball, old microscopes and battlefield surgery kits.

name: National Capital Radio & Television Museum
blurb: A 1906 farmhouse filled with working radios and televisions, from 1920s crystal sets to early color TVs, shown by volunteer guides.

name: Fort Washington Park
blurb: 1824 masonry fort above the Potomac: walk through the sally port, casemates, barracks and gun positions; later concrete batteries dot the grounds.

name: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
blurb: The Hope Diamond and the gem and mineral hall, the Deep Time fossil hall with a T. rex, human origins, mummies and an ocean hall with a giant squid.

name: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
blurb: The 1903 Wright Flyer, Spirit of St. Louis, the Apollo 11 command module and a touchable moon rock. Renovated galleries have been reopening in stages.

name: Smithsonian National Postal Museum
blurb: Under the old City Post Office beside Union Station: airmail planes hanging in the atrium, a railway mail car, Owney the stuffed postal dog and a rare stamp gallery.

name: National Gallery of Art
blurb: The West Building holds the only Leonardo painting in the Americas; a moving walkway through a tunnel of lights leads to the modern East Building.

name: National Museum of Asian Art (Peacock Room)
blurb: Whistler's Peacock Room, a complete blue-and-gold 1870s London dining room, plus ancient Chinese bronzes and jades and Japanese screens.

name: International Spy Museum
blurb: Largest public collection of espionage gear: a lipstick pistol, bugs, an Enigma machine and a Bond Aston Martin, with an undercover-mission game running through it.

name: Eastern Market
blurb: 1873 brick market hall on Capitol Hill with butchers, bakers, cheese, fish and produce stalls and a lunch counter.

name: DAR Museum
blurb: 31 period rooms furnished by state chapters, from a 1690s hall to a 1930s kitchen, plus quilts and decorative arts, in Memorial Continental Hall.

facts.hours: Mon-Fri 10-4, Sat 10-5; closed Sun and federal holidays

name: Smithsonian National Zoo (indoor houses)
blurb: A rainy-day route: Amazonia's indoor rainforest with free-flying birds and an aquarium level, the Reptile Discovery Center and the Small Mammal House.

name: Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center
blurb: Two vast hangars holding Space Shuttle Discovery, an SR-71 Blackbird, the Enola Gay and a Concorde, plus an observation tower and a restoration hangar overlook.

name: National Museum of the Marine Corps
blurb: Walk-through immersive galleries, including a chilled Chosin Reservoir scene and a Vietnam hilltop landing, under a 210-foot tilted spire.

name: National Museum of the United States Army
blurb: Chronological galleries of soldier stories with a Sherman tank, a D-Day Higgins boat and a Huey helicopter, in a stainless-steel building opened in 2020.

facts.reserve: free timed ticket encouraged; walk-ups available

name: Stabler-Leadbeater Apothecary Museum
blurb: Family pharmacy that ran from 1792 to 1933 and was left intact: hand-blown bottles with original contents, and an upstairs room of labeled herb drawers.

facts.hours: Closed Tue year-round and Mon in fall and winter

name: Torpedo Factory Art Center
blurb: Former naval torpedo plant with three floors of open artist studios you can walk into, plus the Alexandria Archaeology Museum upstairs.

name: Colvin Run Mill
blurb: Working c.1811 water-powered gristmill; weekend tours go inside among the wooden gears, and the general store sells the meal it grinds.

facts.hours: Mill tours Sat-Sun; general store Thu-Sun 11-4

name: Lucy Burns Museum at the Workhouse
blurb: Museum of the D.C. prison at Lorton in a former cell block: exhibits on the suffragists jailed here in 1917 and a guided walk through the cells. Art studios fill the old dormitories.

name: DEA Museum
blurb: Free museum inside DEA headquarters on the history of drugs and drug enforcement, from patent medicines and opium dens to cartel cases and seized trafficker items.

name: National Inventors Hall of Fame Museum
blurb: Free museum in the atrium of the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office: a gallery of inductee icons and hands-on displays on patents and trademarks.

facts.hours: Mon-Fri 10-4 plus first Saturday of the month 11-3

name: The Cold War Museum
blurb: Volunteer-run collection on a former Army signals intelligence base: spy cameras, Stasi and Soviet gear, U-2 and Cuban Missile Crisis items.

name: Pope-Leighey House
blurb: Frank Lloyd Wright's 1,200-square-foot Usonian house of cypress, brick and glass, shown by guided tour on the Woodlawn estate.

name: Aldie Mill
blurb: Restored 1807-09 brick gristmill with rare tandem metal waterwheels; volunteers run the machinery and grind grain on open weekends.

facts.hours: Sat-Sun 11-4 in season; closed Nov 2 to Mar 30

name: Museum of the Shenandoah Valley
blurb: Valley history and decorative arts, a gallery of furnished miniature houses and the Glen Burnie house, with seven acres of gardens outside.

name: Hugh Mercer Apothecary Shop
blurb: Costumed guides demonstrate 18th-century medicine in Dr. Hugh Mercer's shop: leeches, lancets, snakeroot and silver-coated pills. Tours start as guests arrive.

name: Blue Ridge Tunnel
blurb: Claudius Crozet's 1858 railroad tunnel, 4,273 feet through the Blue Ridge and unlit: you walk it by flashlight with water dripping from bare rock. Trailheads at both ends.

name: Meems Bottom Covered Bridge
blurb: 204-foot single-span Burr arch bridge of 1894 over the North Fork of the Shenandoah, the longest covered bridge in Virginia and still open to cars.

name: Camera Heritage Museum
blurb: A downtown storefront packed with thousands of cameras, from 19th-century plate cameras to spy and aerial cameras, shown by the people who collected them.

name: Edinburg Mill (Shenandoah Valley Cultural Heritage Museum)
blurb: 1848 mill that survived Sheridan's burning of the valley, now three floors of local history: farm tools, Civil War items and odd community collections.

name: Virginia Museum of the Civil War
blurb: Museum on the 1864 Battle of New Market, where VMI cadets charged, with a film and artifacts; the Bushong farm on the battlefield is outside.
coord_source: wikipedia (New Market Battlefield State Historical Park)

name: National Museum of Civil War Medicine
blurb: Two floors on Civil War medicine: surgical kits, an amputation scene, a field ambulance and embalming, in a building embalmers used after Antietam.

name: Washington County Museum of Fine Arts
blurb: Free art museum in City Park with American paintings, old masters and a glass-roofed courtyard.

name: Hagerstown Roundhouse Museum
blurb: Model train layouts and artifacts from the railroads that met in Hagerstown, with photographs of the demolished Western Maryland roundhouse.

name: Paw Paw Tunnel
blurb: 3,118-foot brick-lined C&O Canal tunnel finished in 1850. Walk the towpath through the dark by flashlight, about half a mile from the parking lot; dry once you are inside.

name: Harpers Ferry Lower Town Museums
blurb: Lower Town's restored buildings hold a string of small museums: John Brown's Fort, a dry goods store, and exhibits on the armory, the raid and the Civil War.

name: Berkeley Springs State Park (Roman Bath House)
blurb: Warm 74-degree mineral springs in a town-square park: soak in a private tub in the 1815 Roman Bath House. A small museum of the springs is upstairs.

facts.hours: Check park for bath hours and prices (not confirmed)

name: Utica Mills Covered Bridge
blurb: 101-foot Burr arch bridge, half of a longer Monocacy River span rebuilt here over Fishing Creek after the 1889 flood. Open to cars.

name: Loys Station Covered Bridge
blurb: 90-foot bridge over Owens Creek, rebuilt on its original timbers after a 1991 arson. Drive through, then stop at the park beside it.

name: Roddy Road Covered Bridge
blurb: Smallest of Frederick County's three covered bridges, a 40-foot kingpost span over Owens Creek, rebuilt after a truck wrecked it in 2016.

name: Museum of the Ironworker (Catoctin Furnace)
blurb: Forensic facial reconstructions of two enslaved furnace workers, iron goods and village history, a short walk from the standing furnace stack.

name: Brunswick Heritage Museum
blurb: A 1,700-square-foot HO-scale model of the B&O line from Washington to Brunswick fills the top floor; railroad town exhibits and C&O Canal displays below.

name: Gettysburg Museum & Visitor Center (Cyclorama)
blurb: The 377-foot Cyclorama painting of Pickett's Charge seen in the round with a diorama foreground, a film and a dozen galleries of battle artifacts.

name: Seminary Ridge Museum
blurb: In the 1832 seminary building that became a field hospital: exhibits on the first day's battle, the care of the wounded and the moral debates behind the war.

name: Sachs Covered Bridge
blurb: 100-foot Town lattice truss bridge of the 1850s, crossed by both armies in 1863. Closed to cars, so you walk through it.

name: Mister Ed's Elephant Museum & Candy Emporium
blurb: Roadside candy store with a museum room of more than 12,000 elephant figurines and oddities, on the Lincoln Highway west of Gettysburg.

name: National Watch and Clock Museum
blurb: More than 12,000 timepieces: tower clocks, automata, pocket watches and the 11-foot Engle Monumental Clock with 48 moving figures.

name: Railroad Museum of Pennsylvania
blurb: Over 100 locomotives and cars, most inside a vast train hall you walk through, with a pit under a steam engine and a window into the restoration shop.

name: Lancaster Central Market
blurb: The country's oldest continuously running public farmers market, in an 1889 brick market house: Amish produce, meats, baked goods and coffee.

facts.hours: Tue, Fri and Sat only, 6 am-3 pm

name: Ephrata Cloister
blurb: Medieval-style Germanic wooden buildings of an 18th-century celibate religious community: the steep-roofed meetinghouse and the Sisters' House with its low doors.

name: Cornwall Iron Furnace
blurb: The only intact charcoal cold-blast furnace complex in the Western Hemisphere. The guided tour goes inside the Gothic furnace building with its great wheel and blast machinery.

facts.hours: Check site for open days (not confirmed)

name: Hunsecker's Mill Covered Bridge
blurb: At 180 feet the longest single-span covered bridge in Lancaster County, over the Conestoga River; rebuilt after Hurricane Agnes took the original.

name: Kurtz's Mill Covered Bridge
blurb: 1876 Burr arch bridge moved into Lancaster County Central Park after Hurricane Agnes; open to cars over Mill Creek.

name: National Civil War Museum
blurb: Two floors covering the war from both sides, with life-size dioramas and a large artifact collection, on the hilltop of Reservoir Park.

name: AACA Museum
blurb: Antique cars set in street scenes from the 1890s to the 1980s, a Tucker collection, and a lower level of buses and a diner.

name: U.S. Army Heritage and Education Center
blurb: Free Army history museum built on soldiers' own letters and gear, with a mile-long outdoor trail of trenches, a firebase and tanks if the rain lets up.

name: National Museum of Industrial History
blurb: In a 1913 Bethlehem Steel shop: huge machine tools shown at the 1876 Centennial, plus steel, silk and propane galleries, beside the blast furnaces.

name: Mütter Museum
blurb: Medical museum of anatomical specimens in wood-and-glass cabinets: the Hyrtl skull collection, the Soap Lady and slides of Einstein's brain.

name: Reading Terminal Market
blurb: Market of 1893 under the old Reading Railroad train shed: about 80 merchants, Pennsylvania Dutch stalls, roast pork sandwiches and scrapple.

name: Wagner Free Institute of Science
blurb: Victorian natural history hall unchanged since the 1890s: 100,000 specimens in original cherry cases, including the first American saber-toothed cat found.

facts.hours: Tue-Fri 9:30-4:30; first Saturday of the month 12-4 (Sept-Dec, Feb-May)

name: Penn Museum
blurb: A 13-ton Egyptian sphinx, the royal tombs of Ur with Queen Puabi's headdress, Egyptian mummies and Maya stelae.

name: Independence Seaport Museum
blurb: Maritime museum with a working boat shop; admission includes the 1892 cruiser Olympia, Dewey's flagship, and the WWII submarine Becuna.

name: Science History Institute
blurb: Free museum of chemistry and alchemy in Old City: early lab glassware and instruments, alchemical paintings and rare books.

name: Brandywine Museum of Art
blurb: Three generations of Wyeths, with N.C. Wyeth's illustrations, in a converted 1864 gristmill with glass-walled lobbies over the Brandywine.

name: Christian C. Sanderson Museum
blurb: One collector's house crammed with oddities: melted ice from the South Pole, sand from the digging of the Panama Canal, Wyeth sketches and battle relics.

name: Newlin Grist Mill
blurb: Water-powered gristmill of 1704, still able to grind, with a guided tour of the wooden gears and millstones; a blacksmith shop is nearby.

facts.hours: Mill tours on weekends at 11, 1 and 2

name: American Treasure Tour Museum
blurb: A tram ride through a former tire factory filled with nickelodeons, band organs, classic cars, store displays and thousands of stuffed animals.

name: Fort Mifflin
blurb: Stone and brick fort on the Delaware beside the airport, besieged in 1777: walk the casemates, bombproofs, powder magazine and barracks as jets come in low overhead.

name: Hagley Museum
blurb: Site of the du Pont black powder works: a visitor center with patent models, a working machine shop and the family's first home. The powder yards are outdoors.

name: Winterthur Museum
blurb: Henry Francis du Pont's 175-room house of American furniture and decorative arts, plus museum galleries; the garden is outdoors.

name: Nemours Estate
blurb: Alfred I. du Pont's 77-room French-style mansion, self-guided, and a chauffeur's garage of vintage cars; formal gardens outside.

name: Delaware Museum of Nature & Science
blurb: Rebuilt and reopened in 2022: a giant squid overhead, dinosaurs, a coral reef under a glass floor and galleries on regional and world ecosystems.

name: Air Mobility Command Museum
blurb: Free: a WWII hangar full of aircraft and exhibits, with big cargo and tanker planes parked outside, some open to walk through.

facts.hours: Wed-Sun 9-4; closed Mon-Tue and most federal holidays

name: Zwaanendael Museum
blurb: Built to resemble the town hall of Hoorn in the Netherlands. Exhibits on Lewes, the wreck of HMS DeBraak and a 'merman' stitched from fish and monkey.

name: Fort Delaware
blurb: Granite and brick Civil War prison fort on Pea Patch Island, reached by ferry from Delaware City: casemates, cells and ramparts with costumed interpreters.

facts.hours: Seasonal: 2026 season ended Sept 27; reopens in spring

name: Fort Miles Museum (Battery 519)
blurb: WWII coastal defense in the dunes of Cape Henlopen: tours go inside Battery 519, a gun battery buried in a dune, with big guns displayed outside.

facts.hours: Check site for Battery 519 tour times (not confirmed)

name: DiscoverSea Shipwreck Museum
blurb: Free museum upstairs from a shell shop: coins, cannon, bottles and thousands of artifacts recovered from Delmarva shipwrecks.

name: Ashland Covered Bridge
blurb: 52-foot Town lattice bridge from about 1860 over Red Clay Creek, open to cars, beside the Ashland Nature Center.

name: Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum
blurb: 18-acre campus: climb inside the 1879 Hooper Strait Lighthouse, watch a working shipyard and tour buildings on oystering, crabbing and waterfowling.

name: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad Visitor Center
blurb: Exhibit hall telling Harriet Tubman's life in the marsh country where she was enslaved, with a film and sculpture; Blackwater refuge is next door.

name: Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge Visitor Center
blurb: Visitor center with eagle and osprey cams, exhibits and an upstairs observatory over the marsh; the Wildlife Drive can be done from the car in rain.

facts.hours: Wildlife Drive closes on some hunt days (Oct 22-23, Dec 4)

name: Wye Grist Mill
blurb: Oldest working mill in Maryland, grinding since 1682; it shipped flour to Washington's army. A small exhibit and the stones and gears inside.

name: Ocean City Life-Saving Station Museum
blurb: 1891 life-saving station at the boardwalk inlet: surf rescue gear, shipwreck artifacts, sands of the world and saltwater aquariums.

name: NASA Wallops Flight Facility Visitor Center
blurb: Free NASA visitor center on sounding rockets, scientific balloons and launches from Wallops, with a rooftop deck facing the launch range.

name: Delmarva Discovery Museum
blurb: Pocomoke River museum with live river otters, a large aquarium of local fish, a walk-in steamboat deck and exhibits on Native people and watermen.

name: Massey Air Museum
blurb: Grass-strip airport with a hangar museum: antique aircraft, a DC-3, engines and a restoration shop.

name: Mermaid Museum
blurb: Small upstairs museum of mermaid lore: a Fiji mermaid, sideshow curios, art and film memorabilia.

name: Gilpin's Falls Covered Bridge
blurb: 119-foot Burr arch bridge of 1860 over North East Creek, the longest covered bridge standing in Maryland. Walk-through only, beside Route 272.

name: Academy Art Museum
blurb: Free art museum partly in an 1820s schoolhouse, with changing exhibitions and a strong collection of works on paper.

name: Calvert Marine Museum
blurb: A megalodon skeleton and Miocene fossils from Calvert Cliffs, river otters and Bay aquariums, a boat shed and the Drum Point screwpile lighthouse you can go inside.

name: Battle Creek Cypress Swamp Sanctuary
blurb: Nature center with live animals, then a quarter-mile boardwalk through one of the northernmost bald cypress stands, at its moodiest in rain.

name: Chesapeake Beach Railway Museum
blurb: Free museum in the 1898 station of the railway that carried Washingtonians to the Bay resort, with photos, models and a surviving passenger car.

name: Patuxent River Naval Air Museum
blurb: Navy flight-test history: simulators, engines and cockpits inside, and more than 20 test aircraft outside, including the X-35C prototype.

name: Historic St. Mary's City
blurb: Maryland's first capital. The St. John's Site Museum is built over a 1638 house foundation; the reconstructed State House and visitor center exhibits. Much is outdoors.

facts.hours: Tue-Sat 10-4 until November; then check site

name: Dr. Samuel A. Mudd House Museum
blurb: Farmhouse where Dr. Mudd set John Wilkes Booth's broken leg in 1865; guided tours show the couch and the bedroom Booth used.
